statements.text: DOGE associates have been feeding vast troves of government records and databases into artificial intelligence tools, looking for unwanted federal programs and trying to determine which human work can be replaced by AI,
statements.venue: Letter to GAO (Huffman and Dexter) on DOGE, as quoted in press release

statements.text: The administration claims we need coal to power AI data centers. Why should a family in California or Ohio foot the bill to keep coal running for the richest tech companies on the planet?
statements.venue: Press release statement on Trump coal handout

statements.text: We need to pump the brakes on the reckless AI buildout, and today’s reporting adds another reason to the pile. Families are already paying higher electric bills to power data centers. Western communities are asking where the water will come from.
statements.venue: Press release statement by Rep. Huffman on data centers on public lands

statements.text: Our Republican colleagues in Congress have fought attempts to put common-sense guardrails on AI data centers. Now we see their endgame: the Trump administration treating our shared natural heritage as a cheap, taxpayer-subsidized dumping ground for massive, energy-guzzling server farms.
statements.venue: Press release statement by Rep. Huffman on data centers on public lands

statements.text: It’s part of the context, for sure. It’s driving a lot of this — we have to be honest about that. This is about data centers and pipelines and grid improvements necessary to meet all this surging demand that’s mostly coming from data centers.
statements.venue: Heatmap News interview on Senate permitting bill and data centers

statements.text: Whatever you think about AI and data centers, we do need that. I’m not going to hold up a chance to improve our grid just because I have big concerns about data centers. I am concerned about how all this huge demand for energy in the next few years is going to be met. If we are stacking the deck for fossil fuel to meet a lot of this demand, that is deeply non-responsive to the climate crisis.
statements.venue: Heatmap News interview on Senate permitting bill and data centers
